title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build an academic career in energy transition and climate sustainability by combining rigorous environmental research, energy systems, climate adaptation, policy analysis, teaching, grants and interdisciplinary leadership.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. research pathway. The first phase develops a defensible research specialization and publication record; the post-Ph.D. phase emphasizes independent research, competitive funding, teaching, doctoral supervision, policy engagement and academic leadership.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Establish expertise in energy systems, climate science, sustainability assessment, adaptation, quantitative methods and environmental policy.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop an independent niche such as renewable-energy systems, climate adaptation, energy policy, carbon management or sustainable infrastructure.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead a research group, supervise Ph.D. students, win interdisciplinary grants and build partnerships with government, industry and communities.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Lead research centres and major programs addressing decarbonisation, resilience, climate finance, energy access and long-term sustainability.

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

The senior academic target is to lead a research program that connects decarbonisation with resilience and development outcomes. Build partnerships across engineering, economics, environmental science, public policy and social science. The strongest long-term profile will be able to evaluate energy transitions not only by emissions, but also by reliability, affordability, equity, resilience and implementation feasibility.
